title: Trading “bot”
author: Zh00_dev
selftext:
Hi! I built an autonomous stock research and portfolio management system focused on S&P 500 stocks, combining quantitative economic theory with LLMs.  
If anyone would like to try it out or share their feedback, here’s the repository:

https://github.com/cve-zh00/alphalab

**P.S.** Over the course of one month, it delivered a 5.8% return (nearly 10 percentage points above the S&P 500).  
**P.P.S.** You can test it using an Alpaca paper trading account. It’s free and easy to set up.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
Alpaca paper trading lets people test this without risking money, but one month's return doesn't establish whether the strategy holds up. I'd include a reproducible paper-trading run with dates, starting allocation, benchmark, turnover and maximum drawdown, plus logs showing what information each LLM decision used. Keep backtests separate from paper results so reviewers can tell which evidence they're judging.

comments.author: spoidercide
comments.body:
I have a quantitative funnel aided by 6 dedicated fine tuned local LLM components that tackle individual autonomous loop functions in rotation... It has resources to find strategies, code them, mutate them orthanologically, optimize them, test them over information bars, fractionally differentiated time framing and so on and so forth

Anyways the goal is to have a selection of strategies it runs combinantly in parallel so that we're never tied to one strategy and it'll solve for regime dependencies and changes.

Really curious about what's going on in your system as the quantitative funneling side of AI trading/building is pretty limited since people want to just make an agent and pray rather than follow a more traditional path.

What I'm asking is if your returns are live or paper so I can perform an audit to see what I can find.

Any additional metrics would help and I'm seeing if theres anything I can incorporate from your structure and feature list or vice versa.

I'm also on git but just listed under private until alpha is finished.

Main thing holding me back is GUI and dry-run wiring needs to be cleaned up but the funnel is done.

here's a short printout of what I've got going on I made to try to break it down maybe feed it into your own system see if theres anything that helps you :

# Quantitative Funnel Architecture & Academic Foundations

1. Universe Screening & Liquidity Filtering
   * Properties & Operations: Dynamic filtering on bid-ask spread stability, minimum volume/order book depth thresholds, and turnover percentiles to eliminate illiquid instruments and minimize implementation shortfall.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Amihud (2002) – "Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects" (Price impact ratios and illiquidity metrics).
      * Pástor & Stambaugh (2003) – "Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns" (Systematic liquidity factor modeling).
2. Feature Engineering & Cross-Sectional Ranking
   * Properties & Operations: Standardized scoring (zzz-scores and percentile ranks) across momentum (time-series and cross-sectional), multi-horizon mean reversion, and market-relative beta.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) – "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers" (Cross-sectional relative-strength anomalies).
      * Fama & French (1993, 2015) – "Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds" / "A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model" (Multifactor risk pricing and anomaly construction).
      * Asness, Moskowitz, & Pedersen (2013) – "Value and Momentum Everywhere" (Pervasive cross-asset factor parity).
3. Signal Generation & Regime Conditioning
   * Properties & Operations: Multi-factor signal aggregation conditional on detected market states (volatility clusters, trend vs. range regimes) to adjust factor tilt weights dynamically.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Hamilton (1989) – "A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle" (Markov-switching regime detection).
      * Ang & Bekaert (2002) – "International Asset Allocation with Regime Shifts" (Regime-dependent covariance and return distributions).
4. Portfolio Construction & Risk Allocation
   * Properties & Operations: Variance-constrained utility maximization, volatility targeting, and downside risk bounds (e.g., CVaR, maximum drawdown limits).
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Markowitz (1952) – "Portfolio Selection" (Mean-variance mathematical optimization).
      * Rockafellar & Uryasev (2000) – "Optimization of Conditional Value-at-Risk" (Convex optimization of tail risk and Expected Shortfall).
      * López de Prado (2016) – "Building Diversified Portfolios that Outperform Out-of-Sample" (Hierarchical Risk Parity / graph-theory clustering).
5. Execution Slicing & Order Routing
   * Properties & Operations: Algorithmic trade schedule optimization (TWAP, VWAP, adaptive limit placement) to minimize execution drag, temporary market impact, and adverse selection.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Almgren & Chriss (2000) – "Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions" (Optimal execution trajectory balancing market impact against inventory risk).
      * Bertsimas & Lo (1998) – "Optimal Control of Execution Costs" (Dynamic programming framework for transaction cost minimization).

# Autonomous LLM Loop, Capabilities & Academic Foundations

1. Unstructured Data Ingestion & Signal Extraction
   * Capabilities & Responsibilities: Continuous extraction of directional sentiment, polarity skew, and material events (earnings disclosures, macro policy, corporate actions) from text streams.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Tetlock (2007) – "Giving Content to Investor Sentiment" (Textual sentiment quantification and market return predictability).
      * Loughran & McDonald (2011) – "When Is a Word Burdensome? A New Measure for Firm Financial Disclosures" (Domain-specific lexicon extraction in financial disclosures).
      * Lopez-Lira & Tang (2023) – "Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models" (LLM zero-shot sentiment predicting equity price shifts).
2. Hypothesis Formulation & Strategy Synthesis
   * Capabilities & Responsibilities: Translation of market observations and quantitative literature into empirical alpha hypotheses, followed by generation of executable code (indicators, factor formulations, test harnesses).
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Miconi et al. (2023) – Research on recursive reasoning agents for autonomous hypothesis discovery.
      * Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) – "Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models" (FunSearch framework for iterative mathematical program and heuristic synthesis).
3. Automated Verification & Backtest Orchestration
   * Capabilities & Responsibilities: Headless dispatch of candidate strategies to deterministic backtest engines to calculate risk-adjusted performance while checking against selection bias and overfitting.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Harvey, Liu, & Zhu (2016) – "...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns" (Controlling data-snooping and multiple-testing errors via Bonferroni/BHY adjustments).
      * Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado, & Zhu (2014) – "The Probability of Backtest Overfitting" (Mathematical quantification of selection bias across multi-trial backtests).
4. Performance Diagnostics & Attribution Feedback
   * Capabilities & Responsibilities: Decomposition of out-of-sample backtest returns, identifying regime mismatches, excessive turnover, or unintended factor exposures, and structuring error traces.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Brinson, Hood, & Beebower (1986) – "Determinants of Portfolio Performance" (Active portfolio return and risk attribution).
      * Shinn et al. (2023) – "Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning" (Self-reflection using structured error traces to guide subsequent trials).
5. Iterative Refinement & Closed-Loop Search
   * Capabilities & Responsibilities: Feeding diagnostic outputs back into prompt context to mutate code, refine mathematical parameters, and re-run evaluations in a closed self-healing loop.
   * Academic Foundations:
      * Wang et al. (2023) – "Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models" (Iterative, closed-loop execution and strategy adaptation).
      * López de Prado (2018) – "Advances in Financial Machine Learning" (Automated quantitative research workflows, defect analysis, and cross-validation integrity).

# Invariant Separation of Responsibilities

* LLM Scope: Operates strictly upstream as an unstructured data parser, alpha hypothesis generator, and diagnostic synthesizer.
* Deterministic Engine Scope: Low-latency execution, position sizing, margin constraints, stop limits, and portfolio optimization remain exclusively governed by rule-based, deterministic mathematical solvers and risk systems.
